meta.about: How the player's guns and arms are drawn: which meshes and animations stand in (soft paths, replaced by the real art without code changes), the gun markers, the base poses, the strike keys, the moving parts and the feel of the additive layers. Everything that decides gameplay is in config.json; nothing here does. Read by MIViewmodel.cpp.
meta.units: web units, as in src/weapon/*.js, converted at load: view space and gun space in metres with x right, y up, z toward the viewer (a gun's muzzle is at -z); angles in radians; Euler angles in the order YXZ (src/weapon/handling.js gunPose). Times in seconds.
meta.sources: src/weapon/viewmodel.js (FEEL, the frame pose), src/weapon/chopper.js and nine.js (markers, poses, strikes, parts), spec 02 sections 2.13, 3.16 and 3.17

firstPerson.note: The arms are the first-person body on the mannequin skeleton, placed each frame so that its bodyHandSocket holds the gun's grip (the gun's 'grip' marker). The real arms keep the skeleton and the socket.

jewels.note: art/out/glb/SK_RuleArms.sockets.json (Blender rest placement, made relative to the bone's reference pose at run time); the watch is not worn on these arms ('worn': false)

opticMaterials.note: base material name -> scalar parameters on the optics in first person (UMIFirstPersonRig): the collimated dot and ring lit to read against a 10,000-nit daylight street (the import's 40 nits drew nothing), the glass nearly clear (0.22 darkened the target). M_TFA_AR_* are the pack's optics, M_Part_Reticle and M_Part_Lens our own red dot and scope (the same parameter names and values; the import makes them from the same recipe as the pack's, with the reticle's axis along +X)

recipe.note: docs/unreal/ANIMATION.md 9: the pack's head joint never moves, so the arms hang from the camera at the eye point (component (0, 0.66, 162.0), +Y forward); first-person field of view 54 (config player.fov.viewmodel) blended by Ads to 38 on the irons and 32 with any optic; near plane 1 cm

rifle.supportElbowDropNote: aimed: the support arm's pole moved this far (arms component space, cm; -Z down) by smoothstep(Ads), the hand kept on the handguard: the forearm drops out of the sight picture

tactical.note: A tactical reload keeps the partly used magazine (ANIMATION.md 9.1 'stow'): it leaves the seat at out and is hidden, no body is dropped; only the empty reload drops one.

rifle.note: docs/unreal/ANIMATION.md 4 and 9: the pack's own first-person clips on SK_RuleArms (no retargeting: the mannequin skeleton) and its weapon clips on the rifle hanging from ik_hand_gun. Reloads: Reload_Quick (tactical) and Reload_Empty played piecewise so the pack's magazine-out, magazine-in and bolt marks (clip seconds) land on the gun's own rule stage times (config / guns.json reload); reserve/out/seated are the clip times of ANIMATION.md 9.1. A gun whose clips or meshes are missing keeps the template way.

pistol.shouldersNote: camera space, cm: the arms' shoulders (midpoint of upperarm_l / _r) under the eye when a solved grip holds the gun (Data/grips.json); the IK reaches both hands from there (console mi.FP.Shoulders "x y z" to try values, "off" for the old wrist slide)

fingerCurl.note: the support hand's fingers only (the bones below hand_l) from the pack's rifle idle, wrapped round a 5 cm handguard as they now wrap the firing hand; optional: without the pack the fingers keep the template pose

grip.note: the hands as art/blender/assets/_rule_grips.py solves them on SK_Nine (Content/Data/grips.json): the wrist and every finger joint as points in the gun's space; the firing palm on the grip with the fingers closed round it and the index on the trigger, the support hand cupping the firing fist, thumbs forward. Applied after the palm IK (MIFirstPersonAnim.cpp ShapeHand / ShapeFingers); the support grip lets go in a reload

pistol.note: The NINE: the engine template's pistol clips (third person, the only pistol clips there are) on SK_RuleArms placed on the gun's grip as before; both palms pulled onto SK_Nine's Palm_R / Palm_L by two-bone IK; the procedural rig poses the gun, its slide, barrel, trigger and magazine (ANIMATION.md 4, 'The NINE').

tracer.note: spec 02 2.8: a placeholder streak (a line) until the Niagara beam exists; colour and speed are config.json weapons.common.tracer

meshOffset.note: SK_Chopper has its origin on the bore at the back of the receiver (the web gun's origin) and its muzzle on +X: the identity, as SK_Nine's. Earlier notes asked for a quarter turn here; that was for a +Y mesh like the pack rifle.

magazine.note: the factory magazine, in the gun's own space (our meshes: the mesh's origin is the gun's, so the part rides the 'magazine' bone); the stage draws it whenever no magazine part is fitted, so a longer one reads as a change; the first person draws it too, and a fitted magazine part replaces it

real.note: docs/unreal/DECISIONS.md 2026-11-25: SK_Chopper is the CHOPPER again (the pack rifle stood in from 2026-11-23). First person is the hand-IK way (animSets.chopper_ik). Merged over this object by the loadout resolver only when realMesh is the mesh drawn; the rules are untouched.

meshOffset.note: where the mesh's own frame sits in gun space. The template rifle (placeholder) has its origin in the grip, its muzzle along +Y and its sight about 16 cm over the grip: it is turned to face -z and lifted so that its sight lies on the CHOPPER's sight line. The real SK_Chopper (origin on the bore at the back of the receiver, muzzle +X) needs pos [0, 0, 0] and rot [0, 0, 0]: see real.meshOffset

sockets.note: grip: GripPoint on the template rifle, Palm_R on SK_Chopper

magazine.note: the factory magazine, in the gun's own space (our meshes: the mesh's origin is the gun's, so the part rides the 'magazine' bone); the stage draws it whenever no magazine part is fitted, so a longer one reads as a change; the first person draws it too, and a fitted magazine part replaces it

real.note: SK_Nine (art/blender/assets/weapons.py: origin on the web gun's origin, muzzle +X, every marker a bone). Merged by the loadout resolver only when realMesh is drawn.

meshOffset.note: as for the CHOPPER: the template pistol has its origin in the grip, muzzle along +Y, rear sight about 12 cm up and 3 cm back; the real SK_Nine needs pos [0, 0, 0]

sockets.note: grip: the Root bone of the template pistol (its origin), Palm_R on SK_Nine; eject: ShellEject on the template, Eject on SK_Nine

enemies.note: How the Vultures are drawn (AMIGoon, AMIBuzzard). Soft paths: the template mannequin with the engine's rifle animation set stands in for SK_Goon_* (docs/unreal/CHARACTERS.md, the mapping of docs/unreal/ANIMATION.md), a basic-shape drone for SK_Buzzard. The actors expose the rule state, events, aim and speed (docs/unreal/GAMEPLAY.md section 7); hit volumes come from config.json, never from the mesh.

weaponOffset.note: CHARACTERS.md: SM_Weapon_GoonSMG's origin is its grip; on bone hand_r at this offset (pitch, yaw, roll degrees), since socket names cannot be set from Python in 5.9

goon.supportGripNote: the left palm's centre on the SMG's SupportHand point (weapons.py socket (0.17, 0, -0.012) m, palm 1.8 cm under it), in the SMG's frame; UMIGoonMeshComponent pulls the left hand there by two-bone IK

lamp.note: src/enemies/goon.js:839, goon-anim.js:367: the lamp follows the rules' want (1.5 + 14 k^2 in the telegraph, 6 in the burst) with damp 30 up, 9 down; a point light stands in for the flare

buzzard.meshNote: SK_Buzzard drawn when it is in the project (tools/box/fp/import-chars.sh): props spun by the rules' rotor angle, the gimbal turned to the eye, the lens lit by the lamp through the eyeMaterial (Color, Intensity); else the placeholder shapes below.

player.note: the player's own flash light (UMIEffects::FlashLight): ahead cm out along the bore past the gun, dimmer and shorter than an enemy's, so it lights the street and not the first-person forearm (review 2026-11-24: the forearm went flat orange-red on every shot)

view.note: the player's own flash (UMIEffects::ViewFlash): cards turned to the eye and pulled toward it to this fraction of their distance (sizes alike), so they draw over the gun's front end that hides the muzzle at the hip; scale on the first-person size. With materials.flashView (depth test off) the player's flash has its own cards that draw over the gun where they are: pullOverlay (1 = on the muzzle) replaces pull and pullAimed

player.note: the player's streak (UMIEffects::PlayerTracer) from the muzzle as drawn to the round's end: cm; its tail never nearer than start past the muzzle, drawn from its first frame

casing.note: UMIEffects::Casing: the player's casing at the first-person depth and size for viewLife s (it leaves the port on screen), then a true-size casing from the port's true place for the rest of life

fx.note: UMIEffects (Weapons/MIEffects.cpp) at the event-bus hooks, on the /Game/FX materials of tools/box/fp/mi_fp_import.py fx: cm, candelas, seconds, linear colours. No material, no effect (a clean checkout).

objectives.note: The master reel cases and the IPX truck (AMIReelCase, AMITruck), placed from level.json objectives and extraction; basic shapes until the props arrive.

art.note: SM_Gameplay_* (art/blender props family): one frame, pivot on the floor, Unreal cm and degrees [pitch, yaw, roll]; the reel of objective i is reels[i]; the lid hinges at the case back edge and opens -95 deg in roll while grabbed. Used when the art is in the project, else the basic shape above.

SM_Vehicle_IPXTruck (pivot on the ground at the truck position, rear toward -X); the vault door leaves on their hinges (manifest notes: Blender (-3.26, +-0.89, 1.05), +-108.9 deg, mirrored into Unreal). Drawn in every map once the art is in the project.

explosives.note: What an explosive shows when it is gone (spec 02 2.13: low, inside the footprint, no collision). `mesh`: the prop art drawn as modelled (pivot on the foot) and then `wreck` is art too (no scaling); without the art in the project, the basic shape scaled to the box and the wreck scaled by wreckHeight.

block.note: The block at run time (AMIBlockGeometry): every level.json collider becomes collision in every map; it is drawn as grey boxes only in a map without art (no actor tagged artTag).
block.startPitchNote: Degrees, up positive: the view's pitch when a run puts the player on the start (UMIGameSubsystem::ResetPlayer). The start position and heading stay the web game's; at pitch 0 the open trash can 1.1 m ahead (prop 270, collider 704, kept for the golden walks) filled the bottom of every run's first frame.
